experiment_description: Analytical Floquet-evolution calculation for the central mechanism of the paper: a many-body interacting quantum kicked-rotor model in which each rotor is tuned to a quantum resonance and the dynamics is controlled by the symmetry of the effective kicking potentials under partial π translation. The dimensionless Hamiltonian is H=sum_{j=1}^N tau_j p_j^2/2 + V(theta_1,...,theta_N) sum_n delta(t-n), with hbar=T=1, integer momentum eigenvalues p_j, angular coordinates theta_j, and one-step operator U=exp[-i sum_j tau_j p_j^2/2] exp[-i V(theta)]. For this calculation, q rotors in the index set S are at the secondary resonance tau_j=2*pi and all other rotors are at the principal resonance tau_j=4*pi. The partial translation maps theta_j to theta_j+pi for j in S and leaves the other coordinates unchanged; the transformed coordinate vector is theta'. For wavepacket dynamics, the initial state is an arbitrary pure state psi(0), and D_j(t)=<p_j(t)-p_j(0)> and sigma_j^2(t)=<[p_j(t)-p_j(0)]^2> are evaluated after integer kick number t. V_j(theta) denotes the part of V containing theta_j; V_{j+}=[V_j(theta)+V_j(theta')]/2 and V_{j-}=[V_j(theta)-V_j(theta')]/2. The averages <...> are over the initial coordinate-space probability density |<theta|psi(0)>|^2. The quantities alpha_{j±}=<-partial V_{j±}/partial theta_j>, lambda_{j±}=<(partial V_{j±}/partial theta_j)^2>, and kappa_j=<(partial V_{j+}/partial theta_j)(partial V_{j-}/partial theta_j)> are defined from that initial-state average. For bipartite entanglement, the N rotors are partitioned into subsystem A and complement B, with V=V_A(theta_A)+V_B(theta_B)+V_I(theta_A,theta_B). Linear entropy is S_lin=1-Tr(rho_A^2). The interaction symmetry components are V_{I±}=[V_I(theta)+/-V_I(theta')]/2. For independent coordinate variables theta_A, theta_B, theta_A', and theta_B', define epsilon_±=V_{I±}(theta_A,theta_B)+V_{I±}(theta_A',theta_B')-V_{I±}(theta_A',theta_B)-V_{I±}(theta_A,theta_B'), and the average of trigonometric functions is over the product of the initial subsystem coordinate probability densities. The calculation is configured to classify the predicted wavepacket and entanglement regimes without choosing a special functional form of V.

mean_momentum_displacement_D_j_formula.description: The analytical expression for the rotor-resolved mean momentum displacement after t kicks.
mean_momentum_displacement_D_j_formula.result: D_j(t)=t*alpha_{j+} for even t=2m; D_j(t)=t*alpha_{j+}+alpha_{j-} for odd t=2m+1

mean_squared_momentum_displacement_sigma.description: The analytical expression for the rotor-resolved mean-squared momentum displacement after t kicks.
mean_squared_momentum_displacement_sigma.result: sigma_j^2(t)=t^2*lambda_{j+} for even t=2m; sigma_j^2(t)=t^2*lambda_{j+}+2*t*kappa_j+lambda_{j-} for odd t=2m+1

linear_entropy_S_lin_formula.description: The exact analytical expression for bipartite linear entropy after t kicks.
linear_entropy_S_lin_formula.result: S_lin(t)=1-<cos(t*epsilon_+)> for even t=2m; S_lin(t)=1-<cos(t*epsilon_+)*cos(epsilon_-)>+<sin(t*epsilon_+)*sin(epsilon_-)> for odd t=2m+1

short_time_asymmetric_linear_entropy_for.description: The leading short-time expansion of bipartite linear entropy for an interaction containing both translation-symmetric and translation-antisymmetric components.
short_time_asymmetric_linear_entropy_for.result: S_lin(t)≈(<epsilon_+^2>/2)*t^2 for even t=2m; S_lin(t)≈(<epsilon_+^2>/2)*t^2+<epsilon_+*epsilon_->*t+(<epsilon_-^2>/2) for odd t=2m+1

experiment_description: Numerical Floquet simulation of the two-rotor kicked-rotor model used to illustrate the paper's symmetry-selection mechanism connecting wavepacket spreading and entanglement. The kicking potential is V(theta_1,theta_2)=k_1 cos(theta_1)+k_2 cos(theta_2)+xi cos(theta_1-theta_2), with k_1=0.1, k_2=0.2, and xi=1. Rotor 1 is set at the principal quantum resonance tau_1=4*pi and rotor 2 at the secondary quantum resonance tau_2=2*pi; hbar=T=1. The initial state is the product momentum eigenstate |p_1=0> tensor |p_2=0>. The bipartition for entanglement is rotor 1 versus rotor 2, and linear entropy is S_lin=1-Tr(rho_1^2). The simulation evaluates <p_1^2(t)> over kick steps shown on a logarithmic time axis up to t=1000, and <p_2^2(t)> and S_lin(t) over kick steps up to t=100. The central concept tested is that the partial π translation of the secondary-resonant rotor makes the rotor-1 effective potential mixed-symmetry, the rotor-2 effective potential antisymmetric, and the inter-rotor coupling antisymmetric, so the measured quantities target hybrid, anti-resonant, and entanglement-oscillatory responses respectively.

experiment_description: Numerical Floquet simulation of the same two-rotor kicked-rotor potential V(theta_1,theta_2)=k_1 cos(theta_1)+k_2 cos(theta_2)+xi cos(theta_1-theta_2), now with k_1=2, k_2=3, and xi=0.1. Both rotors are tuned to the secondary quantum resonance tau_1=tau_2=2*pi, with hbar=T=1. The initial state is |p_1=0> tensor |p_2=0>, and the entanglement bipartition is rotor 1 versus rotor 2 with linear entropy S_lin=1-Tr(rho_1^2). The wavepacket variances <p_1^2(t)> and <p_2^2(t)> and the linear entropy are evaluated over integer kick steps up to t=1000. This setup tests the central claim that when both rotors undergo the partial π translation, the single-rotor effective potentials have mixed symmetry while the inter-rotor coupling is symmetric, producing mixed wavepacket spreading but initially quadratic entanglement growth before saturation.

experiment_description: Numerical Floquet simulation of a symmetry-broken variant of the two-rotor kicked-rotor model. The baseline potential is V(theta_1,theta_2)=k_1 cos(theta_1)+k_2 cos(theta_2)+xi cos(theta_1-theta_2) with k_1=2, k_2=3, and xi=0.1, and an additional inter-rotor term cos(2*theta_1-theta_2) is included in the kicking potential. Both rotors are at the secondary resonance tau_1=tau_2=2*pi, with hbar=T=1. The initial state is |p_1=0> tensor |p_2=0>, the bipartition is rotor 1 versus rotor 2, and S_lin=1-Tr(rho_1^2) is evaluated for kick steps up to t=1000. The setup targets the paper's central mixed-symmetry mechanism by adding an interaction component that is neither purely symmetric nor purely antisymmetric under the partial π translation.

linear_entropy_dynamical_regime.description: The classified dynamical regime of bipartite linear entropy under the added symmetry-breaking interaction.

experiment_description: Numerical Floquet simulation of an extended two-rotor kicked-rotor model containing higher angular harmonics, used to test that the central symmetry mechanism does not depend on the specific low-harmonic potential form. The kicking potential is V(theta_1,theta_2)=k_1 cos(2*theta_1)+k_2 cos(2*theta_2)+xi cos(2*theta_1-theta_2), with k_1=k_2=0.1 and xi=1. Both rotors are tuned to the secondary resonance tau_1=tau_2=2*pi, hbar=T=1, and the initial state is |p_1=0> tensor |p_2=0>. The bipartition for entanglement is rotor 1 versus rotor 2, and linear entropy is S_lin=1-Tr(rho_1^2). The simulation evaluates <p_1^2(t)> and <p_2^2(t)> up to t=100 and S_lin(t) up to t=100. Under the partial π translation, the coupling term is antisymmetric while each rotor effective potential is mixed-symmetry, so the setup targets simultaneous hybrid wavepacket spreading and period-2 entanglement dynamics.

experiment_description: Numerical Floquet simulations of higher-order-resonance two-rotor kicked-rotor models without imposing the special translational potential symmetry needed for the analytic high-order solution. The potential is V(theta_1,theta_2)=k_1 cos(theta_1)+k_2 cos(theta_2)+xi cos(theta_1-theta_2), with k_1=9, k_2=10, and xi=0.1. The initial state is |p_1=0> tensor |p_2=0>, hbar=T=1, and the bipartition is rotor 1 versus rotor 2 with linear entropy S_lin=1-Tr(rho_1^2). Three resonance-order pairs are simulated: tau_1=4*pi/3 with tau_2=4*pi/5, tau_1=4*pi/13 with tau_2=4*pi/15, and tau_1=4*pi/19 with tau_2=4*pi/21. The time sweep covers integer kicks up to t=1000. This setup characterizes how the central quantum-resonance wavepacket mechanism persists while entanglement changes when wavepacket splitting, proliferation, and interference occur in higher-order resonances.

p2_variance_time_exponent.description: The power-law exponent of the rotor-2 momentum variance growth versus kick number in the simulated higher-order resonances.

linear_entropy_initial_time_exponent.description: The power-law exponent of the initial bipartite linear entropy growth before saturation in the simulated higher-order resonances.

linear_entropy_dynamical_regime.description: The classified dynamical regime of bipartite linear entropy for the high-order-resonance simulations.

experiment_description: Robustness numerical simulations for the central resonance-controlled dynamics under weak detuning away from exact quantum resonance. The two-rotor potential is V(theta_1,theta_2)=k_1 cos(theta_1)+k_2 cos(theta_2)+xi cos(theta_1-theta_2), with k_1=2, k_2=3, and xi=0.1. The exact-resonance reference has rotor 1 at tau_1=4*pi and rotor 2 at tau_2=2*pi; detuned simulations use tau_1=4*pi+delta_tau_1 and tau_2=2*pi+delta_tau_2, where the offsets are incommensurate with 4*pi. The initial state is |p_1=0> tensor |p_2=0>, hbar=T=1, and linear entropy is computed for the rotor-1/rotor-2 bipartition. For the direct comparison, delta_tau_1=delta_tau_2=10^-3 and <p_1^2(t)>, <p_2^2(t)>, and S_lin(t) are compared to the exact-resonance trajectories up to t=100. For the scaling analysis, delta_tau_1=delta_tau_2=delta_tau is swept over 10^-3, 5*10^-4, 10^-4, 5*10^-5, and 10^-5. The deviation measure is Delta_1=|<p_1^2>_0-<p_1^2>|/<p_1^2>_0, where <p_1^2>_0 is the exact-resonance value. The agreement time t_D is defined as the kick number at which Delta_1 reaches a 1% threshold.

agreement_time_steps_for_delta_tau_1e_mi.description: The approximate kick number up to which the detuned and exact-resonance trajectories remain in agreement for equal detunings of 10^-3.

relative_deviation_time_exponent.description: The power-law exponent of the time growth of the rotor-1 relative deviation over the early detuning-sensitive interval.

agreement_time_detuning_scaling_exponent.description: The fitted exponent relating the 1% agreement time to equal detuning strength.

undetuned_odd_step_linear_entropy.description: The odd-kick value of the exact-resonance period-2 bipartite linear entropy for the reference system.

experiment_description: Numerical simulation of the many-body kicked-top counterpart introduced to test whether the kicked-rotor central mechanism transfers to finite spherical phase space. The model contains two quantum tops with total angular momentum quantum number j_tot=50. The kick operator is U_k=exp[-i sum_{n=1}^2 beta_n J_{nz}^2/(2*j_tot)], and the between-kick Hamiltonian is H_f=alpha_1 J_{1x}+alpha_2 J_{2x}+(alpha_12/j_tot) J_{1x}J_{2x}+(alpha_122/j_tot^2) J_{1x}J_{2x}^2. The parameters are alpha_1=0.0001, alpha_2=0.02, alpha_12=0.005, and alpha_122=0.0005. Top 1 is at the principal kicked-top resonance beta_1=4*pi*j_tot, and top 2 is at the secondary resonance beta_2=2*pi*j_tot. The initial state is |J_{1z}=0> tensor |J_{2z}=0>. The bipartition is top 1 versus top 2, and linear entropy is S_lin=1-Tr(rho_1^2). The simulation tracks the normalized variances <J_{1z}^2>/j_tot^2 and <J_{2z}^2>/j_tot^2 and S_lin over kick numbers up to about 10^4. The setup targets the kicked-top analogue of the mixed-symmetry resonance mechanism, while accounting for the finite spherical phase-space bound on wavepacket spreading.

j1z_wavepacket_dynamical_regime.description: The classified dynamical regime of the top-1 angular-momentum variance before finite-phase-space saturation.

j2z_wavepacket_dynamical_regime.description: The classified dynamical regime of the top-2 angular-momentum variance before finite-phase-space saturation.

linear_entropy_dynamical_regime.description: The classified dynamical regime of bipartite linear entropy in the kicked-top simulation.

wavepacket_variance_saturation_scale_for.description: The finite spherical phase-space scale at which kicked-top wavepacket variance ceases unbounded growth.
